parsed.main_gap: The refinement lemma’s graph argument incorrectly infers that every component is a tree from the global inequality e<q.

errors.description: A graph with fewer edges than vertices may still contain a cyclic or loop component alongside tree components. Thus the arbitrarily selected component containing a_q need not be bipartite. Repair: choose a component with e_C<v_C; connectedness then gives e_C=v_C-1, so it is a tree.
errors.quote: Having fewer edges than vertices, the graph contains no cycle and no loop, since a cycle or a loop on v vertices already uses at least v edges; hence every connected component C has e_C=v_C-1 and is a tree

parsed.notes: The flaw is local and straightforwardly repairable. After selecting an actually acyclic component, the discrepancy bound works, and the drafting lemma, refinement construction, subset-sum bound, and binary lower-bound strategy form an essentially complete proof.
